sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Howell County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Howell County splits the work between two offices on Court Square in West Plains. The Collector, listed as Janet Crow on the collector's site, is in Room 201 of the Howell County Office Building, 35 Court Square, at (417) 256-4001. The Assessor, Daniel Franks, is down the hall in Suite 202 at (417) 256-8284.

The collector is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm and stays open at noon. The assessor's site lists weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm and offers GIS mapping and a subscription parcel search. The collector prepares separate statements for personal property, real estate and utilities, so a homeowner with a truck and a house gets more than one bill.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Howell County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The collector's site says statements go out in November and are due on receipt. They become delinquent after December 31, and a payment must carry a postmark of December 31 or earlier or it comes back unprocessed unless late fees are included. If no statement arrives by the end of November, call right away, because a missing statement does not cancel the tax or any penalty and interest.

sections.h2: What does the Howell County assessor say about who owes tax?
sections.html:
The assessor's general information page cites RSMo 137.075: whoever owns or holds property on January 1, including a buyer who closed that day, is liable for that calendar year's tax. Its example is a person who leaves Missouri in June 2026. That person was assessed on January 1, 2026 and still pays Missouri tax for 2026, because the law makes no provision for prorating the bill.

That page speaks to vehicles and other personal property, which owners must list with the assessor before March 1. For a house sale, the contract and the closing statement decide how real estate tax is shared between seller and buyer, so read that section of your contract before you sign.

sections.h2: How is a Howell County home valued for tax?
sections.html:
State law assesses residential real property at 19 percent of true value, farmland at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent. RSMo 137.115 sets those rates and has the assessor reset real estate values every odd-numbered year.

  • An increase above 15 percent for a home, without new construction, calls for a physical inspection of the property.
  • The owner may ask for an interior look and has at least thirty days to say so.
  • On appeal, the assessor carries the burden of proof for increases of that size under RSMo 138.060.

Open the assessor's parcel search at howell.missouriassessors.com to see your parcel record before you call.

sections.h2: What can I do if I disagree with my Howell County value or tax bill?
sections.html:
The State Tax Commission describes a two-step path. File with the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. After the Board decides, you have 30 days from the date on its letter to bring a complaint to the Commission. A stipulated value you sign with the assessor ends the case.

You can also pay under protest. RSMo 139.031 requires the whole bill to be paid before the delinquency date, a written statement of grounds filed with the collector, and a suit against the collector in circuit court within ninety days. The disputed portion is held in a separate fund until the case ends. Taxes paid by mistake can be credited or refunded if you apply within three years of payment.

sections.h2: When is the Howell County tax sale, and how do I stop one?
sections.html:
The collector holds its delinquent tax sale on the fourth Monday in August each year, which matches RSMo 140.150. Under that statute you may pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector at any time before your land is sold. The collector must first mail notice to the record owner, and a notice that never arrives does not erase the debt.

If you plan to sell, ask the collector at (417) 256-4001 for a payoff on the parcel and pass it to the title company. Ask the title company to pay any balance from the sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How did Howell County get its name and its records?
sections.html:
The county is named for Josiah Howell, a settler who bought the first settlement in Howell Valley. A small wooden courthouse went up on the West Plains square in 1859 and burned in 1862, and an 1869 courthouse followed, described as a three-room frame building about 24 by 30 feet. The county was reorganized in 1865, and all of its records were lost in an 1866 fire.

The 2020 census found a median age of 41.5, with 21.0 percent of residents 65 or older. About 70.2 percent of residents lived in rural areas and 67.2 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.

sections.h2: What should a Howell County seller know about the area and its housing?
sections.html:
Howell County is in south-central Missouri along the Arkansas line. It was organized on March 2, 1857, and the courthouse burned in 1862. West Plains is the county seat and largest city, with Brandsville, Mountain View and Willow Springs among the other cities. At 927 square miles of land it ranks third in Missouri by land area, and part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside it.

  • Population: 40,798 estimated for July 1, 2025
  • Housing units: 18,288, with 15,965 households
  • Owner-occupied rate: 70.3%
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $173,000
  • Median gross rent: $733
  • Median household income: $50,993, with 18.6% of people below the poverty line
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 67

Public school districts include West Plains R-7, Willow Springs R-IV, and Mountain View-Birch Tree R-III, along with several smaller rural districts. Median travel time to work is 23.1 minutes, per the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Howell County?
faqs.a: Pay the Howell County Collector at 35 Court Square, Room 201 in West Plains, online, by phone at 1-800-652-0405 for current taxes, by mail or in the drop box outside the office building. Walk-in hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the Howell County tax deadline?
faqs.a: Statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. A mailed payment needs a postmark of December 31 or earlier, or it is returned unless late fees are included.

faqs.q: Does Howell County prorate tax if I move away mid-year?
faqs.a: No. The assessor explains that tax is based on what you owned on January 1, and the law makes no provision for prorating it. For a home sale, your contract and closing statement decide how the buyer and seller split the bill.

faqs.q: When does Howell County sell land for delinquent tax?
faqs.a: The collector holds the sale on the fourth Monday in August. You can pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector before the sale to keep the property.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Howell County assessment?
faqs.a: File with the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. If the Board rules against you, appeal to the State Tax Commission within 30 days of the Board's decision letter. Call the assessor at (417) 256-8284 first to ask for a review of your parcel record.
